title: Is zero point two the same as zero point two zero?
description: A place table settles the zero dilemma between two friends and then finds the smallest and largest of 0.2, 0.20, 0.200, 0.02 and 0.002. Keeko doubts that 0.20 equals 0.2 and thinks the longer decimal is bigger.
teaching_notes: One idea: a zero at the right end of the decimal part holds no quantity, so the value does not change. Watch for students who think more digits mean a bigger number.

source: Use a place table to settle Sonu and Zara, and then say whic
video_script.why: The child can read decimals by place value and now decides when two different looking decimals are equal.
video_script.substitution: Write each decimal in a place table, and compare the quantity in each place.
video_script.anchor: the place table of the book with the rows 0.2, 0.20, 0.200, 0.02 and 0.002
video_script.wrong_answer: zero point two zero is bigger
video_script.wrong_move: Says 0.20 is bigger than 0.2 because it has more digits.
video_script.payoff_line: A zero at the right end adds nothing

final_answer.value: 0.2, 0.20 and 0.200 are equal; the smallest is 0.002
final_answer.spoken: zero point two, zero point two zero and zero point two zero zero are equal; the smallest is zero point zero zero two

names.{{NAME_1}}: says 0.2 can be written as 0.20 and 0.200
names.{{NAME_4}}: thinks zeros on the right may change the value

hold_back: 0.2, 0.20 and 0.200 are equal; the smallest is 0.002
maths_rules: all three are 2 tenths, so they are equal
video_script.design: The book's place table stays on screen. Rows light up one at a time, and the tenths column keeps one colour.

<bookmark mark='more'/>The other two are zero point zero two, and zero point zero zero two.

marks.a: zero point two fills its row
marks.b: zero point two zero fills its row

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, fill the place table. Zero point two has two in the tenths place.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Zero point two zero has two tenths and zero hundredths.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Zero point two zero zero has two tenths, and zeros after that.

beats.on_screen: all three rows show 2 tenths, so 0.2 = 0.20 = 0.200

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step two, compare the three rows. Each one shows two tenths and nothing more.
<bookmark mark='right'/>They stand for the same quantity, so {{NAME_1}} is right.

marks.h: the two sits in the hundredths column
marks.th: the two sits in the thousandths column

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step three, zero point zero two is two hundredths.
<bookmark mark='th'/>Zero point zero zero two is two thousandths. These are different quantities.

marks.ends: the largest and the smallest are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>Step four, two tenths is more than two hundredths, and that is more than two thousandths.
<bookmark mark='ends'/>The largest is zero point two, and the smallest is zero point zero zero two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 0.2, 0.20 and 0.200 are equal; the smallest is 0.002

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A zero at the right end adds nothing.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>Zero point two, zero point two zero and zero point two zero zero are equal.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The smallest is zero point zero zero two.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.long: a longer decimal is not always bigger

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks zero point two zero is bigger, since it has more digits.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But zero point two zero has two tenths and no hundredths at all.
<bookmark mark='long'/>A longer decimal is not always a bigger one.
